389	
390	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
391	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
392	
393	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
394	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
395	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
396	    """
397	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
398	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
399	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
400	        if field not in bundle:
401	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
402	    source = bundle["source"]
403	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
404	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
405	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
406	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
407	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
408	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
409	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
410	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
411	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
412	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
413	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
414	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
415	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
416	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
417	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
418	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
419	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
420	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
421	
422	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
423	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
424	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
425	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
426	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
427	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
428	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
429	    for name, entry in sources.items():
430	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
431	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
432	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
433	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
434	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
435	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
436	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
437	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
438	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
439	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
440	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
441	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
442	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
443	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
444	    return source, candidate

447	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
448	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
449	
450	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
451	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
452	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
453	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
454	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
455	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
456	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
457	    """
458	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
459	    if not present:
460	        return
461	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
462	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
463	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
464	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
465	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
466	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
467	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
468	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
469	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
470	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
471	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
472	    for item in state_proofs:
473	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
474	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
475	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
476	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
477	        proof = item["proof"]
478	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
479	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
480	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
481	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
482	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
483	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
484	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
485	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
486	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
487	        ):
488	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
489	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
490	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
491	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
492	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
493	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
494	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
495	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
496	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
497	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
498	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

501	# -- stage 2/3: trust, expiry and signature -----------------------------------
502	
503	
504	def _authenticate(
505	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
506	) -> None:
507	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
508	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
509	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
510	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
511	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
512	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
513	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
514	
515	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
516	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
517	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
518	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
519	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
520	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
521	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
522	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
523	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
524	
525	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
526	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
527	    if public_key is not None:
528	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
529	        if signature is None:
530	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
531	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
532	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
533	        ):
534	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
535	        return
536	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
537	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
538	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
539	    if signature is not None:
540	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)

543	# -- stage 4: chain recomputation and response cross-check --------------------
544	
545	
546	def _tip_descriptor(blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
547	    tip = blocks[-1]
548	    return {
549	        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
550	        "height": tip.height,
551	        "length": len(blocks),
552	        "status": tip.status,
553	    }

555	
556	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
557	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
558	
559	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
560	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
561	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
562	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
563	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
564	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
565	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
566	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
567	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
568	    """
569	    blocks: list[Block] = []
570	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
571	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
572	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
573	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
574	        height = block_raw.get("height")
575	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
576	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
577	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
578	        status = block_raw.get("status")
579	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
580	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
581	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
582	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
583	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
584	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
585	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
586	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
587	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
588	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
589	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
590	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
591	        if height != position:
592	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
593	        expected_prev = (
594	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
595	        )
596	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
597	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
598	        if position == 0:
599	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
600	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
601	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
602	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
603	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
604	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
605	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
606	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
607	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
608	
609	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
610	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
611	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
612	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
613	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
614	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
615	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
616	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
617	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
618	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
619	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
620	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
621	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
622	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
623	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
624	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
625	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
626	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
627	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
628	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
629	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
630	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
631	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
632	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
633	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
634	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
635	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
636	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
637	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
638	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
639	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
640	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
641	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
642	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
643	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
644	        if recomputed != block_hash:
645	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
646	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
647	        # the comparison decisions above.
648	        try:
649	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
650	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
651	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
652	    return blocks

655	def _check_candidate_summary(candidate: object, descriptor: dict) -> None:
656	    """Cross-check an export-format candidate's own tip summary fields.
657	
658	    A bare block list has nothing to check. A five-field export document's
659	    supplied ``tip_hash/height/length/status`` must equal the recomputed tip
660	    descriptor, exactly as the node requires on resubmission.
661	    """
662	    if not isinstance(candidate, dict):
663	        return
664	    for field in DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS:
665	        if field in candidate and candidate[field] != descriptor[field]:
666	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
667	
668	
669	def _check_response(response: dict, descriptor: dict) -> None:
670	    """Every descriptor field present in the response must equal the tip's.
671	
672	    A response carrying none of the descriptor fields cannot be bound to the
673	    recomputed chain at all, so it is rejected rather than vacuously accepted.
674	    """
675	    matched = False
676	    for field in DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS:
677	        if field in response:
678	            matched = True
679	            if response[field] != descriptor[field]:
680	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
681	    if not matched:
682	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

685	def _check_state_anchor(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
686	    """Bind the state extension's anchor to the recomputed candidate chain.
687	
688	    ``state_height`` must name a confirmed candidate block whose hash equals
689	    ``state_block_hash``; an unknown height, a pending block or a hash
690	    mismatch is an integrity failure. Every state-proof item and document
691	    must agree with both anchor heights, the bundle's state root and the
692	    anchor block hash.
693	    """
694	    height = bundle["state_height"]
695	    state_root = bundle["state_root"]
696	    block_hash = bundle["state_block_hash"]
697	    if height >= len(blocks):
698	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
699	    block = blocks[height]
700	    if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.block_hash != block_hash:
701	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
702	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
703	        proof = item["proof"]
704	        if item["height"] != height or proof["height"] != height:
705	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
706	        if proof["state_root"] != state_root or proof["block_hash"] != block_hash:
707	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

710	# -- stage 5: proofs ----------------------------------------------------------
711	
712	
713	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
714	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
715	
716	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
717	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
718	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
719	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
720	    """
721	    verified: list[str] = []
722	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
723	    for item in proofs_raw:
724	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
725	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
726	        height = item.get("height")
727	        proof = item.get("proof")
728	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
729	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
730	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
731	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
732	        block = blocks[height]
733	        if block.height != height:
734	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
735	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
736	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
737	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
738	
739	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
740	        index = proof.get("index")
741	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
742	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
743	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
744	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
745	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
746	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
747	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
748	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
749	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
750	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
751	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
752	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
753	
754	        key = (height, tx_id)
755	        if key in seen:
756	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
757	        seen.add(key)
758	
759	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
760	            tx_id,
761	            proof.get("siblings"),
762	            block.merkle_root,
763	            block.block_hash,
764	            block.block_hash,
765	        ):
766	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
767	        verified.append(tx_id)
768	    return sorted(verified)
769	
770	
771	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
772	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
773	
774	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
775	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
776	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
777	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
778	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
779	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
780	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
781	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
782	    ascending.
783	    """
784	    height = bundle["state_height"]
785	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
786	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
787	    accounts: set[str] = set()
788	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
789	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
790	            continue
791	        for tx in block.transactions:
792	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
793	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
794	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
795	
796	    verified: list[str] = []
797	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
798	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
799	        proof = item["proof"]
800	        account = proof["account"]
801	        expected = position.get(account)
802	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
803	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
804	        # failure.
805	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
806	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
807	        key = (item["height"], account)
808	        if key in seen:
809	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
810	        seen.add(key)
811	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
812	            proof,
813	            bundle["state_root"],
814	            height,
815	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
816	        ):
817	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
818	        verified.append(account)
819	    return sorted(verified)

1066	def _validate_range_trust(trust: object) -> None:
1067	    """Structural validation of the trust document's ``sources``/``allowlist``.
1068	
1069	    Mirrors the bundle verifier's trust rules; a ``genesis_hash`` is not
1070	    required here because the caller pins the range anchor directly. The
1071	    optional GET /v1/trust ``source_key_history`` mapping is validated too:
1072	    each source maps to a non-empty ascending array of
1073	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` items whose versions are
1074	    dense from 1 with strictly ascending activation ids, both numeric fields
1075	    non-boolean positive integers and the public key 64 lowercase hex.
1076	    """
1077	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
1078	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1079	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1080	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
1081	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1082	    for name, entry in sources.items():
1083	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
1084	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1085	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
1086	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1087	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1088	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
1089	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1090	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1091	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1092	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
1093	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1094	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
1095	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
1096	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1097	    history = trust.get("source_key_history")
1098	    if history is not None:
1099	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
1100	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1101	        for name, entries in history.items():
1102	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
1103	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1104	            if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
1105	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1106	            last_activated = None
1107	            for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
1108	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(
1109	                    _HISTORY_ENTRY_KEYS
1110	                ):
1111	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1112	                version = entry.get("version")
1113	                public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1114	                activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
1115	                # Versions are dense from 1; both numeric fields are plain
1116	                # (non-boolean) positive integers.
1117	                if not _is_int(version) or version != position + 1:
1118	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1119	                if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1120	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1121	                if not _is_int(activated) or activated < 1:
1122	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1123	                if last_activated is not None and activated <= last_activated:
1124	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

1133	def _authenticate_range_export(document: dict, trust: dict, now: float) -> None:
1134	    """Check mode-specific source authorization and every deadline.
1135	
1136	    A ``plain`` export is only acceptable from an allowlisted source and must
1137	    carry ``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authorized one of
1138	    two ways:
1139	
1140	    * the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping (the new
1141	      rule): the source must appear in the mapping — the historical public key
1142	      matching and signature verification happen by attestation version in
1143	      :func:`_verify_range_attestation`; the trust ``sources`` entry and its
1144	      deadline play no role, so a delivery signed under a since-rotated or
1145	      revoked key still authenticates as long as the document itself is
1146	      unexpired;
1147	    * the mapping is absent (the legacy rule): the source must be a
1148	      ``sources`` entry whose unexpired deadline is checked.
1149	
1150	    All deadlines are checked before any integrity work: an expired,
1151	    correctly-signed export is still unusable.
1152	    """
1153	    source = document["source"]
1154	    mode = document["mode"]
1155	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1156	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1157	    if mode == "plain":
1158	        if source not in allowlist:
1159	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1160	        # A plain export carrying an attestation is not a plain delivery.
1161	        if document["attestation"] is not None:
1162	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1163	    elif _has_key_history(trust):
1164	        # Historical-key authorization: the source (and later the attestation
1165	        # version) must resolve in the mapping; the current registry entry is
1166	        # deliberately not consulted.
1167	        if source not in trust["source_key_history"]:
1168	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1169	    elif source not in sources:
1170	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1171	
1172	    if document["expires_at"] <= now:
1173	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1174	    if mode == "plain":
1175	        if allowlist[source] <= now:
1176	            raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1177	    elif not _has_key_history(trust) and sources[source]["expires_at"] <= now:
1178	        # Legacy rule only: the pinned registry entry's own deadline applies.
1179	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)

1182	def _recompute_range_tail(anchor: dict, blocks_raw: list) -> list[Block]:
1183	    """Recompute and validate the delivered tail standalone from the anchor.
1184	
1185	    Mirrors the node's own range-tail rules: heights run consecutively from
1186	    ``anchor.height + 1``, the first ``prev_hash`` is the anchor hash and
1187	    later ones link internally, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
1188	    signature verifies, tx_ids are unique across the tail and ascending
1189	    inside each block, Merkle roots and block hashes recompute, and a pending
1190	    block may only sit at the tail tip. Every field is checked on the *raw*
1191	    JSON value; type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height,
1192	    non-positive or non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while
1193	    recomputation mismatches stay ``integrity``.
1194	    """
1195	    blocks: list[Block] = []
1196	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1197	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(blocks_raw):
1198	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
1199	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1200	        height = block_raw.get("height")
1201	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
1202	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
1203	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
1204	        status = block_raw.get("status")
1205	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
1206	        # Same rule as the whole-chain recomputation: a height of the wrong
1207	        # type or sign is a field-type defect (input), never coerced.
1208	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
1209	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1210	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
1211	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1212	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
1213	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1214	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
1215	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1216	        if height != anchor["height"] + 1 + position:
1217	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1218	        expected_prev = (
1219	            anchor["block_hash"] if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
1220	        )
1221	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
1222	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1223	        if position < len(blocks_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
1224	            # A pending block may only sit at the tail tip.
1225	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1226	
1227	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
1228	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
1229	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
1230	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1231	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
1232	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
1233	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
1234	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
1235	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
1236	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
1237	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1238	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
1239	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1240	            # The raw amount must already be a non-boolean positive integer —
1241	            # never a coercible string, float or bool.
1242	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
1243	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1244	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
1245	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1246	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
1247	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
1248	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
1249	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1250	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
1251	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1252	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
1253	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1254	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
1255	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
1256	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
1257	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1258	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
1259	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1260	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
1261	        if recomputed != block_hash:
1262	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1263	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
1264	        # the comparison decisions above.
1265	        try:
1266	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
1267	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
1268	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
1269	    return blocks

1290	def _verify_range_attestation(document: dict, trust: dict) -> None:
1291	    """Verify the attested export's Ed25519 signature under the pinned key.
1292	
1293	    Two rules, selected by the trust document:
1294	
1295	    * with ``source_key_history`` present, the attestation's ``version``
1296	      selects the source's historical public key; the source not appearing in
1297	      the mapping, or the attestation version not being one of its dense
1298	      versions, is an authorization failure (``auth``), as is a mismatch
1299	      between the attestation's ``public_key`` and that historical key. The
1300	      Ed25519 signature is then checked over the SHA-256 digest of the
1301	      canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message — a wrong signature is an
1302	      integrity failure. The attestation's version is already structurally
1303	      guaranteed to be a positive integer.
1304	    * without the mapping (legacy rule), the attestation's ``public_key``
1305	      must be exactly the key the trust document pins in ``sources`` for the
1306	      source (a mismatched credential is an authorization failure) and the
1307	      same signature check follows.
1308	    """
1309	    source = document["source"]
1310	    attestation = document["attestation"]
1311	    if _has_key_history(trust):
1312	        history = trust["source_key_history"].get(source)
1313	        if history is None:
1314	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1315	        version = attestation["version"]
1316	        # Versions are structurally guaranteed dense from 1, so a valid
1317	        # version simply indexes the ascending history.
1318	        if version < 1 or version > len(history):
1319	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1320	        pinned = history[version - 1]["public_key"]
1321	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1322	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1323	    else:
1324	        pinned = trust.get("sources", {})[source]["public_key"]
1325	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1326	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1327	    message = attested_range_message(
1328	        source,
1329	        document["request_id"],
1330	        document["expires_at"],
1331	        document["anchor"],
1332	        document["blocks"],
1333	        document["tip"],
1334	    )
1335	    digest = hashlib.sha256(message).digest()
1336	    if not crypto.verify_signature(pinned, digest, attestation["signature"]):
1337	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

"""Offline light-client verification of externally supplied proof bundles.

A proof bundle lets a client verify ledger responses without trusting the
serving node or holding any chain state:

    bundle = {
        "source": str,
        "expires_at": int,            # Unix seconds
        "response": object,           # the attested response object
        "candidate": [...],           # full block list starting at genesis
        "proofs": [                   # optional Merkle inclusion proofs
            {"height": int, "proof": {height, tx_id, index, merkle_root,
                                      block_hash, siblings}},
            ...
        ],
        # Optional account-state extension: all four fields are either present
        # together or absent together, and state_proofs is a non-empty list.
        "state_root": str,            # 64 lowercase hex, anchored state root
        "state_height": int,          # confirmed anchor block height
        "state_block_hash": str,      # 64 lowercase hex anchor block hash
        "state_proofs": [             # account-state inclusion proofs
            {"height": int, "proof": {account, balance,
                                      confirmed_transactions, index,
                                      state_root, height, block_hash,
                                      siblings}},
            ...
        ],
        "signature": str,             # optional Ed25519 signature hex
    }

The local trust document pins the genesis block hash and records, per source,
an optional Ed25519 public key with its own expiry, plus an allowlist of
sources accepted without signatures:

    trust = {
        "genesis_hash": "<64 lowercase hex chars>",
        "sources": {source: {"public_key": hex, "expires_at": int}},
        "allowlist": {source: expires_at_int},
    }

Verification, in order:

1. **input** — bundle and trust must have the documented shape; every numeric
   field must be a plain (non-boolean) integer.
2. **auth** — the source must be trusted (a ``sources`` entry or the
   ``allowlist``). A source with a public key must sign the bundle; a bundle
   carrying a signature for a key-less source, or an unsigned bundle from a
   non-allowlisted source, fails.
3. **expired** — neither the bundle deadline nor the trust entry's deadline
   may have passed (``expires_at <= now`` counts as expired).
4. **integrity** — the signature (when required) is verified over
   Ed25519(sha256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle without
   ``signature``)); the candidate chain is recomputed from the pinned genesis
   (heights, prev_hash linkage, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
   signature, unique tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes, pending-only-at-tip)
   and the response's descriptor fields are checked against the recomputed
   tip descriptor ``S``.
5. **proof** — every proof must be unique, its tx_id/height/index and block
   fields must agree with the candidate block, the Merkle path must verify
   under the existing rules, and its block must not be the pending tip. When
   the state extension is present, its anchor (``state_height`` /
   ``state_block_hash``) must name a confirmed candidate block (integrity) and
   every state proof must agree with both anchor heights, the state root and
   the anchor hash; each account must sit at its ``index`` in the ascending
   account set of the anchor height's confirmed transactions, ``height`` +
   ``account`` pairs must be unique, and every proof must pass
   ``crypto.verify_account_proof`` against the bundle's anchors.

On success :func:`verify_bundle` returns
``{"ok": True, "source", "S", "verified_tx_ids"}`` — plus
``"verified_accounts"`` (ascending) when the state extension was verified —
on failure ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
``input/auth/expired/integrity/proof``.

:func:`verify_range_export` verifies one exported incremental range delivery
(the ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` document, top-level key order
``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip, attestation``)
offline against a caller-pinned expected anchor and the local trust document.
The expected anchor must strictly equal the document's ``anchor``; the
delivered tail is recomputed standalone from that anchor (consecutive
heights, prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures,
unique and block-ascending tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes,
pending-only-at-tip) and the closed ``tip`` summary must recompute. A
``plain`` export must come from an unexpired ``allowlist`` entry and carry
``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authenticated by key
version: when the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping,
the attestation's ``version`` selects that source's historical public key
(which must equal the attestation's ``public_key``); an unknown source or
version, or a mismatched key, is ``auth`` and a signature that fails to
verify is ``integrity`` — so an export signed under a since-rotated key
stays verifiable. A trust document without ``source_key_history`` keeps the
legacy rule: the source must be an unexpired ``trust.sources`` entry whose
pinned key matches the attestation and verifies the Ed25519 signature over
the SHA-256 digest of the canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message.
Failures map to ``input`` (structure), ``auth`` (authorization), ``expired``
(deadlines) and ``integrity`` (anchor/chain/signature); nothing is raised.
Success returns ``{"ok": True, "source", "request_id", "mode", "anchor",
"tip", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending.

:func:`verify_range_exports` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
range deliveries as one continuous chain. The first page's anchor must equal
the caller-pinned ``expected_anchor``; every later page's anchor must equal
the previous page's closed tip's ``{height, block_hash}``. Each page is
re-verified under the same input/auth/expired/integrity rules, transaction
ids are unique across the whole batch, and a pending block may only appear on
the last page — a broken anchor, a height jump, a duplicate transaction or any
block after a pending one is an ``integrity`` failure. Success returns
``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``tip``
the last page's tip, ``pages`` the page count and ``verified_tx_ids``
ascending; failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one
of ``input/auth/expired/integrity``.

:func:`verify_header_page` verifies one signed ``GET /v1/chain/headers``
page offline. The document has the exact top-level key order
``anchor, headers, tip, auth``: a closed ``{height, block_hash}`` anchor, an
ascending list of ``{height, prev_hash, merkle_root, block_hash, status}``
headers (no transactions), the chain descriptor S and an
``{key_version, signature}`` envelope. The caller pins both the anchor and
the tip hash; ``trust.audit_signers`` supplies the public key selected by
``key_version``. Key-order/type defects are ``input``; an unknown key
version or a failed Ed25519 verification over
``SHA256(UTF8("ledger-headers-v1") || canonical_json(document without
auth))`` is ``auth``; an anchor/tip mismatch, a recomputed header hash or
prev_hash link mismatch, a non-consecutive height, or a pending header
anywhere but the chain tail is ``integrity``. An empty page is valid only
when its anchor is the pinned tip. Success returns
``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "verified_block_hashes"}``; nothing is
raised for malformed input.

:func:`advance` durably checkpoints a verified batch to ``path``. The
checkpoint file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with the exact declared key
order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash`` and a single trailing
newline (non-ASCII written unescaped); ``generation`` starts at 1 and
increments per successful advance, ``anchor``/``tip`` are the batch's pinned
anchor and closed tip, ``context`` has the exact key order
``verified_at, trust, documents, verified_tx_ids`` (the ``now`` at verification,
the trust document and the re-verifiable batch verbatim) and ``state_hash`` is
the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact) JSON of the other four fields.
The first advance requires a legal ``anchor``; later advances accept ``None``
(continue from the stored tip) or the stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``.
Verification itself is :func:`verify_range_exports` unchanged. Same-path
advances share one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a
failed verification never bumps the generation. An existing checkpoint is
strictly reloaded (key order, types, state hash and a context replay at its
``verified_at``); any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never
truncated or rebuilt. Failures return only ``{"ok": False, "error":
category}`` with category one of
``input/auth/expired/integrity/state/io``; success appends the new
``generation`` as the final result key.

Every successful :func:`advance` also maintains a generation-history sidecar
at ``path + ".history"``: one compact UTF-8 JSON document (same serialization
rules as the checkpoint) with the exact top-level key order
``v, base, records, head``. ``v`` is 1; ``base`` is ``{generation, hash}``
naming the generation *before* the first retained record; each record is
``{checkpoint, prev, hash}`` where ``checkpoint`` is the persisted five-key
checkpoint document, ``prev`` is the previous record's hash (the first
record's is ``base.hash``) and ``hash`` is
``SHA256(ASCII(prev) || canonical_json(checkpoint))``; ``head`` is the last
record's hash. Record generations run consecutively from
``base.generation + 1``. A fresh path starts from ``base = {0, Z}`` (Z = 64
zeros); a pre-existing generation-``g`` checkpoint without a sidecar is
treated as ``base = {g-1, Z}`` with that checkpoint as the first record, and
later advances append. Both files are written under the same per-path lock as
one transaction: an ``io`` failure restores the original bytes best-effort
(a failed compensation surfaces as ``state`` on the next read); crash
atomicity across the two files is not guaranteed.

:func:`history` reads (and prunes) the sidecar. ``history(path)`` returns
``{"ok", "base", "record", "head", "kept"}`` with ``record`` the last
generation's record and ``kept`` null; ``generation=`` selects one retained
generation (an absent one is a ``state`` failure). ``keep=n`` (mutually
exclusive with ``generation``; both must be non-boolean positive integers)
retains only the last ``min(n, count)`` records: when nothing is pruned the
file's bytes are untouched, otherwise ``base`` becomes the last pruned
record's ``{generation, hash}`` and the sidecar is rewritten (the checkpoint
file itself never changes). Loading replays every retained generation —
shape, state hash, context replay and anchor continuity — so any tampering
is a ``state`` failure; a missing or unreadable sidecar is ``io``.

:func:`export_history` exports the retained sidecar pages as signed,
offline-verifiable page documents. ``export_history(path, key, after=None,
limit=50, trust_path=None)`` strictly reloads both the checkpoint and its
sidecar under the shared per-path lock and returns one page with the exact key
order ``base, records, next, head, checkpoint, auth``: ``base``/``records``
are the sidecar's own documents (nested key orders unchanged), ``head`` the
sidecar head, ``checkpoint`` the persisted five-key checkpoint (identical to
the last retained record's), ``next`` the page's last record generation when
another page follows or ``null`` on the final page, and ``auth`` is
``{public_key, signature}`` where the Ed25519 signature is made by the 64-hex
seed ``key`` over the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact,
unescaped-non-ASCII) JSON of the page with ``auth`` removed. ``after`` is
``None`` (start after ``base``) or a non-boolean non-negative integer naming
either ``base.generation`` or a non-last retained generation; ``limit`` is a
non-boolean integer in 1..200. Bad arguments are ``input``, a missing or
unreadable file ``io`` and a corrupt checkpoint/sidecar or unmatched cursor
``state``. With ``trust_path`` set to a signer log (see
:func:`history_trust`), the log is strictly loaded first (a missing log is
``io`` and a corrupt one ``state``) and the page is truncated to the longest
prefix, starting at the cursor, whose checkpoints all carry the same key
active at their ``verified_at``: it stops just before the first record that
would straddle an authorization boundary and sets ``next`` (non-null) so the
following page continues there. The seed ``key`` must derive to the public
key covering that whole span — an unknown or revoked covering key is an
``auth`` failure. A page ending exactly at the retained tail still closes
with ``next: null``.

:func:`verify_history` verifies an ordered, non-empty list of such pages
offline against one pinned 64-hex Ed25519 ``public_key``. Every page must have
the exact key order and nested types; ``base``, ``head``, ``checkpoint`` and
the signing public key must be identical on every page; each Ed25519 signature
must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. Records must run
consecutively from ``base.generation + 1`` and link across page seams through
each page's ``next`` (a non-final page's ``next`` is its last record
generation), every record hash is recomputed and every checkpoint is replayed
(state hash plus the stored batch context) with anchor continuity. The final
page alone carries ``next: null``, its last record's hash must equal ``head``
and its checkpoint must equal the page checkpoint; missing, duplicate or
reordered pages and any tampering are rejected. Success is ``{"ok": True}``;
failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
``input`` (structure/types), ``auth`` (pinned key or signature) and
``integrity`` (chaining, pagination or checkpoint replay); nothing is raised.

:func:`verify_history_trust` verifies the same pages against a signer
rotation/revocation log instead of one pinned page key, so each page's
``auth.public_key`` may differ. The ``trust`` document has the exact key
order ``root, records, head``: ``root`` is a 64-hex Ed25519 key that must
equal the pinned ``root`` argument; every non-empty record has the exact key
order ``at, key, status, prev, signature`` with ``at`` a plain
(non-boolean) positive strictly-ascending integer, ``key``/``prev`` 64
lowercase hex, ``status`` exactly ``active``/``revoked`` and ``signature``
128 lowercase hex. The first ``prev`` is 64 zeros, every later one is the
previous record's canonical-JSON SHA-256 and ``head`` is the last record's
hash; each certificate is the root key's Ed25519 signature over the
SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON with ``signature`` removed. An
``active`` record authorizes ``key`` from its ``at`` until the next record;
a ``revoked`` one withdraws it until a later ``active``. A page must name
the single key active at every checkpoint ``verified_at`` it carries — a
page straddling an authorization boundary is rejected — and its signature
must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. All page structure,
chaining, pagination and checkpoint-replay rules stay identical to

page signature, an unknown or revoked page key) and ``integrity`` (``at``
not ascending, a bad ``prev``/``head``, a boundary crossing, or any
record/pagination/checkpoint-replay defect); nothing is raised and success
is ``{"ok": True}``.

:func:`history_trust` persists such a signer log at its own file path.
``history_trust(path)`` strictly loads and returns the ``{root, records,

or all absent — with ``root_seed`` a 64-hex Ed25519 seed (its public key is
the log root), ``at`` a non-boolean positive integer, ``key`` a 64-hex public

``active``; ``at`` must strictly ascend; a ``revoked`` entry must name the
currently active key; re-appending the current tail's ``at``/``key``/

newline serialization and atomic per-path-locked replace as the checkpoint
files, and a failed write restores the original bytes best-effort.
